newsitem.title: USA: PC stocks hit by IBM downgrade, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: PC stocks hit by IBM downgrade, profit-taking.

text.p: The stocks of personal computer makers slid Thursday after Salomon Brothers lowered its rating for industry giant International Business Machines Corp. and investors took advantage of a recent rally in technology issues, traders said.
"It's probably a combination of IBM (being downgraded) and just some profit-taking," said Patrick Davis, head of over-the-counter trading at Salomon Brothers.
"The computer systems makers are off, and IBM is a part of that," said Greg Nie, senior vice president of technical research at Everen Securities.

IBM fell $1.625 to $88.50 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Dell Computer Corp. lost $2.625 to $113 on Nasdaq. Compaq Computer Corp. fell $3.50 to $103.25, Gateway 2000 Inc. dropped $4 to $70.375 on the NYSE, and Micron Technology Inc. slipped 50 cents to $42.625, also on the NYSE.

"It's partly IBM, as well as some concern about consumer demand for PCs," said Vadim Zlotnikov, an analyst with Sanford Bernstein. "There's also been quite a run-up (in share prices) lately, so there's some profit-taking going on."
Gateway, a direct marketer of personal computers, is among the most vulnerable to concerns about PC demand, and its stock was hardest hit, analysts said.
The American Stock Exchange computer index lost 2.03 points, or 0.48 percent, to 423.67.
Earlier Thursday, Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones cut his rating on IBM to buy from strong buy.
Despite the downgrade, Jones said he remains positive about IBM's long-term factors and believes the stock could rise to $100 over the next nine months.
